eyebrow: Initializing against the right target profile
caption: A hardware-oriented profile is more restrictive than the default simulator profile — catch the mismatch locally, before submission.

code:
results = qsharp.run("PrepareAndMeasure()", shots=1000)
# results is a Python list of 1000 outcomes, e.g. ['Zero', 'One', 'Zero', ...]
caption: The idiomatic way to collect many shots once you're past a one-off sanity check and into real experiment code.

eyebrow: Resource estimates, then a real submission
code:
estimate = qsharp.estimate("MyAlgorithm()")
print(estimate)   # physical qubits, runtime, logical qubits, error budget

from azure.quantum import Workspace
workspace = Workspace(subscription_id="<id>", resource_group="rg-quantum-dev",
                       name="qsharp-dev-workspace", location="eastus")
job = workspace.submit(qsharp_program, target="ionq.simulator", shots=1000)
caption: qsharp handles local compilation and simulation; azure-quantum handles cloud submission — same compiled program, both.
